Activation.description: The activation of a catalogued mode by a study.

effect_step.description:
How the mode's effects follow its state: absent, at once; with
`zero_delay` or `instant`, one step later, through an automaton
`<mode>__effect` whose transition follows the mode's occurred state
with a zero delay or an instantaneous law of probability one. The
step is what a PyCATSHOO external mode does: its effects ride on a
mirror automaton one zero-delay step behind the mode.

instances.description: The instances it applies to; exclusive with `type`.

metadata.description: Free editor data, never read by the expander.

mode.description: Mode name in the type's catalogue.

repair.description: Repair law; absent means the mode, once occurred, stays occurred.

repair_condition.description:
A repair condition: the repair cannot complete while it is false
(a guard on the repair edge only, never on the occurrence or an
on-demand re-arm). Same grammar as `condition`; requires `repair`.

type.description: Every instance of this type; exclusive with `instances`.

AggOp.description:
Aggregation over the values connected to an *in* port
(sum, count, all, any, mean, median).

oneOf.description: True iff all connected boolean values are true.
True iff at least one connected boolean value is true.

Arithmetic mean of connected numeric values (M3: sensor
averaging: cod3s `compute_reference_mean`). 0.0 with no
connection.

Median of connected numeric values (M3: redundant-sensor
median/vote). Even count averages the
two central values; 0.0 with no connection.

Analyses.description:
Analyses a study requests, each written with the parameters of the
Python function that runs it (the model aside), which `pyraichu` checks
when it loads the study.

AttrRef.description:
Reference to an attribute by hierarchical name: the *authoring /
serialized* form. Build-time validation resolves it to dense indices
(typed errors on dangling references; no stringly-typed lookups at
simulation time).

attribute.description: Name of the attribute inside the component.

component.description: Name of the component owning the attribute.

oneOf.description: Negation (exactly one argument; enforced by model validation).

CommonCauseGroup.description:
A common-cause group: a mode catalogued on every member's type, failing
the members together by combination. Each active order `k` gives one
automaton per combination of `k` members, named after their 1-based
positions in `instances` (`cc_1_2`), in a component named after the
group; a combination holds every member it covers with the catalogued
effects.

effect_step.description:
With a step, each member's effects follow the combinations covering
it one step behind, through an automaton `<group>__effect` on the
member, and a combination occurs only with its members' steps at
rest and is repaired only once they have taken hold: a PyCATSHOO
external common-cause mode. Without, effects are immediate.

instances.description: The members, in order: their positions name the combinations.

metadata.description: Free editor data, never read by the expander.

mode.description: The catalogued mode it fails its members with.

name.description: Group name, also the name of its generated component.

orders.description: One entry per active order; an absent order builds no combination.

Condition.description: A condition: a core expression in which `mode_active` names an activated mode as `Instance.mode`.

oneOf.description: Aggregate the values connected to an in-port.

channel.description:
Optional **channel selector**. Absent (the default) reads the
attribute each connected out-port exports: its single, shared
value. Present, it reads instead the per-connection quantity
the compiler materialises for that channel, so two consumers
on the same out-port receive different numbers (the
conservative-flow shape). Every connected out-port must
declare the named channel; validation refuses otherwise.

args.description: Operands (`Not` takes exactly one; validated at model build).

oneOf.description:
True while the referenced automaton is in the given state:
muscadet links state changes to attribute changes through it.

Conditional expression: with [`Expr::StateActive`] as condition
it covers the piecewise-by-automaton-state right-hand sides of
the corpus (empty/full tank freezing `dv/dt`).

Natural exponential `e^arg` (state-dependent failure rates:
the heated-tank λ(T) of the Aldemir benchmark).

Current simulation time (M4). Meaningful in continuously
evaluated expressions (equations, watched margins, guards);
sensitive functions are *not* re-triggered by the passage of
time alone.
True while the named mode is occurred.

Distrib.description:
Occurrence distribution of a transition (M0 deterministic subset; `Exp` and the
wider distribution library arrive in milestone M2).

oneOf.description:
Deterministic delay: fires `time` after the source state is
entered. Exactly one target state.

Instantaneous branching: fires immediately;
the destination is drawn among `targets` with the given
probabilities. `probs` holds N−1 values for N targets, the last
probability being the complement `1 − Σ probs`.

probs.description: First N−1 branch probabilities, each in [0, 1], Σ ≤ 1.

oneOf.description:
Watched transition (paper rule `schedule_boundary`, M1): fires exactly when
the continuous trajectory makes its guard become true. The guard
is the boundary predicate: it must contain at least one ordering
comparison (`<`, `≤`, `>`, `≥`) between float expressions,
possibly composed with and/or/not and discrete gates, so the
engine can locate the crossing by root-finding on the signed
margin. Exactly one target state.

Exponential distribution (paper rules `schedule_stochastic` and `reschedule_modifiable`): a
spontaneous PDMP jump with survival
`P(T > t) = exp(−∫₀ᵗ λ(x(u)) du)`. Exactly one target state,
and exactly one of the two rate forms:

- `rate`: fixed positive λ; the firing date is sampled as
  `t + Exp(λ)` at source-state entry (`schedule_stochastic`). Memoryless: a
  guard turning true re-arms with a fresh draw.
- `rate_expr`: **state-dependent** λ(x) as an expression. The
  engine realises the survival integral with a cumulative
  hazard: a threshold `E ~ Exp(1)` is drawn at source-state
  entry and the transition fires when `∫ λ dt` reaches `E`.
  When λ depends only on discretely-updated state the hazard is
  piecewise-constant and the firing date is rescheduled at each
  discrete change (`reschedule_modifiable`); when it depends on
  ODE-integrated attributes (or time), the hazard is integrated
  alongside the continuous state and the firing time is located
  like a watched boundary crossing. λ must evaluate ≥ 0.

rate.description: Fixed occurrence rate λ > 0 (events per time unit).

rate_expr.description:
State-dependent occurrence rate λ(x) ≥ 0 (events per time
unit), evaluated on the current model state.

oneOf.description: Weibull distribution (M4): delay sampled with CDF `1 − e^{−(t/scale)^shape}`.

sigma.description: Standard deviation of the underlying normal (> 0).

oneOf.description: Uniform distribution (M4): delay drawn uniformly in `[low, high)`.

Empirical / user-defined distribution (M4): inverse-CDF sampling from a
table of `(time, cumulative probability)` points: any
distribution supplied as a sampled CDF. `u < points[0].1` maps
to `points[0].0` (probability mass at the first time); between
points the CDF is linearly interpolated; the last cumulative
probability must be 1.

FearedEvent.description: A feared event: a generated component watching a condition.

metadata.description: Free editor data, never read by the expander.

name.description: Event name; it becomes the component name.

target.description: Whether reaching the event ends and labels a sequence.

tempo_not_occ.description:
How long the condition must fail before the event clears: a delay
(a number) or a timed law.

tempo_occ.description:
How long the condition must hold before the event occurs: a delay
(a number) or a timed law.

GroupOrder.description: The laws of one order of a common-cause group.

order.description: How many members a combination of this order fails together.

repair.description: Repair law; absent means a combination, once occurred, stays so.

oneOf.description: Observe an attribute's value over time.
Observe whether an automaton is in a given state (0/1 over time).

Observe the **truth of a threshold** on an attribute: `true` while
`attr cmp value` holds, `false` otherwise.

The difference with [`IndicatorTarget::Attribute`] is the whole
point of the variant, and it is a difference of *quantity*, not of
spelling: on a free-valued attribute the sojourn of
[`IndicatorTarget::Attribute`] is the time-integral of the value
(an area), while the sojourn here is the **time spent under the
condition** (a duration, bounded by the horizon). A study that
asks "how long was there hydrogen in the tank" asks for the
second, and reading it off the first returns the tank's content
integrated over time, which is plausible, larger than the horizon,
and silently the wrong question's answer.

`value` is a constant: this carries the threshold a study
declares (cod3s's `operator` / `value_test` pair), not a general
expression. Kinds are checked at build time, so a boolean
attribute may only be tested for (in)equality and a numeric one
may not be compared to a boolean.

value.description: The constant the attribute is compared against.

name.description: Indicator name (unique in the model; any length is accepted).

InterruptionPolicy.description:
What happens to a pending occurrence countdown when the transition
guard turns false (naming set by Roland, 2026-07-04). Only
meaningful for duration distributions (delay, exp, …) with a guard.

oneOf.description:
The occurrence duration is cancelled; a fresh duration is drawn
as soon as the guard holds again (interruptible transition).
RAICHU's default.

The countdown is paused and resumes where it stopped when the
guard holds again: a RAICHU extension, e.g. suspended repair
work.

The countdown never stops: the transition fires at the drawn
date even if the guard dropped meanwhile
(pinned by the `interrupt_01` cross-validation).

Nature.description:
The nature of a mode. It serves selection and reporting and changes
no semantics.

OneOffMode.description: A mode the study declares on one instance only.

effect_step.description:
How the mode's effects follow its state: absent, at once; with
`zero_delay` or `instant`, one step later, through an automaton
`<mode>__effect` whose transition follows the mode's occurred state
with a zero delay or an instantaneous law of probability one. The
step is what a PyCATSHOO external mode does: its effects ride on a
mirror automaton one zero-delay step behind the mode.

effects.description: Effects on targetable attributes of the instance.

metadata.description: Free editor data, never read by the expander.

name.description: Mode name, unique on its instance.

repair_condition.description:
A repair condition: the repair cannot complete while it is false
(a guard on the repair edge only, never on the occurrence or an

PortRef.description: Reference to a port by hierarchical name (authoring form).

component.description: Name of the component owning the port.

port.description: Name of the port inside the component.

Quantification.description:
One quantification of a study: the probability that `target` is the
first declared target reached by `horizon`, answered by `method`.

instants.description:
Reporting instants of the methods that draw at random, ascending,
within `[0, horizon]`. Default: the horizon alone.

seed.description: Master seed of the methods that draw at random.

target.description: Name of a target the system or the study declares.

QuantificationMethod.description:
A quantification method and its settings, written as the
quantification envelope records it. The expander types the name; the
settings belong to the method and are checked against it by the
quantification contract (`raichu_quantify::Method::from_parts`), which
`pyraichu` applies when it loads the study.

settings.description: The method's settings; a setting left out takes its default.

QuantificationMethodName.description:
A quantification method, by the name the quantification envelope
records (`raichu-quantify`).

oneOf.description: Monte-Carlo simulation stopped at the targets.
Exact exploration of the sequence tree (Markov family).
Discretised exploration of the sequence tree.
Biased Monte-Carlo with factors fitted by cross-entropy.

Simulation.description:
Run settings of a study, plain data mapped onto the engine's runs by
the caller.

options.description:
The run's other keywords, named as the Python entry point names
them (`pyraichu.monte_carlo` or `pyraichu.run_sequences`):
confidence, quantiles, thread count, solver tolerances, flow policy.
`pyraichu` checks them against that entry point when it loads the
study.

stop_at_targets.description: Stop each replica at the first target reached.

StateRef.description: Reference to an automaton state by hierarchical name (authoring form).

component.description: Name of the component owning the automaton.

StudyDocument.description: A study: which modes run, with which laws, and what is observed.

common_cause_groups.description:
Common-cause groups: a catalogued mode failing several instances
together, one law per order.

metadata.description: Free editor data, never read by the expander.

one_off_modes.description: Modes declared for one instance only.

quantification.description: A quantification of a target by one of the quantification methods.

system.description: The system the study applies to, by name.

targets.description: Sequence-analysis targets, in the core form.

Target.description:
A **sequence-analysis target** (feared event / événement redouté): a
named automaton state whose activation ends and labels a trajectory's
recorded sequence (mirrors cod3s `endCause`). Empty `targets` = no early
stop and no `end_cause` (the trajectory runs to `t_max`).

state.description: The state whose activation reaches the target.

Tempo.description:
The confirmation time of a feared event: a fixed delay, or a timed law
written as a core law object.

Value.description:
A runtime value carried by attributes and expressions.

M0 kinds only: booleans, integers, floats. `String` discrete state is
reserved (a deliberate departure) and will extend this enum
without breaking serialized models (tagged representation).
